well: ODP Holes 170-1039B (incoming-plate reference, seafloor -4,353.5 m, 99.5% recovery), 170-1040C (prism toe above the decollement, -4,177.9 m; sample 21R-6 at 356.6 mbsf) and 205-1253 (Leg 205 return to the incoming plate, -4,376.3 m; sample 3R at 385.2 mbsf) - COSTA RICA SUBDUCTION COMPLEX, Middle America Trench, North Pacific (9.64-9.66 N, 86.18-86.20 W), the catalogue's first EROSIVE convergent margin
operator_on_log: Ikari, Niemeijer, Spiers, Kopf & Saffer (MARUM/Utrecht/Penn State) laboratory friction experiments at ELEVATED pressure AND temperature (effective normal stress 15-90 MPa, pore pressure 10-61 MPa, temperature 19-212 C); drilling by JOIDES Resolution on Legs 170 (1996) and 205 (2002); the catalogue's fourth Ikari-lab entry - the discipline now spans FOUR subduction zones (Nankai, Japan Trench, Hikurangi, Costa Rica)
source_database: PANGAEA, dataset doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.834641 ('Strength measurements from ODP Hole 170-1039B, 170-1040C and 205-1253'), in series doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.834645; supplement to Ikari et al. 2013, Geology 41(8), 891-894 (doi:10.1130/G33956.1)

coverage: COMPLETE DATASET: 31 measurement rows from 6 experiments on 3 samples - paired room-temperature and hydrothermal (stepped 53-212 C) friction ladders at effective normal stresses 15-90 MPa: clay-rich Leg 170 material (incoming hemipelagics 1039B-9H3, prism-toe 1040C-21R-6) friction coefficient 0.21-0.48, versus Leg 205-1253 carbonate-rich material at 0.71-0.88 with peak shear strengths to 70.2 MPa - the catalogue's highest-stress and highest-temperature friction conditions

Event rides as per-row quality; Exp + Sample label verbatim in file
source_anomaly_disclosure: THREE source quirks preserved verbatim: (1) the parameter named 'Shear strength (µpeak)' carries NO unit in the header and a friction-coefficient-style mnemonic, but it is peak SHEAR STRENGTH in MPa - proven by re-deriving tau = mu x sigma_n_eff on all 31 rows (worst deviation 0.0056, within the 2-decimal rounding of the published mu); (2) the ten 1039B rows have NO archived depth (geocode and top/bottom all empty - the archive gives only core designation 9H3), so those rows load with NaN index values, carried as the archive left them; (3) experiment u048 runs SIX stress steps (from 15 MPa) while the other five experiments run five (from 30 MPa) - the asymmetry is real and is exactly what closes the header's own 237-point Size declaration (10x7 + 10x9 + 11x7)
purpose: thirty-third catalogue entry - COSTA RICA / MIDDLE AMERICA TRENCH joins as region TWENTY-ONE (the first erosive margin, completing the subduction quartet with accretionary Nankai, post-seismic Japan Trench, and slow-slip Hikurangi) and the elevated-P/T friction envelope is kind TWENTY-TWO: not soft-sediment strength (kind 18), not slip-event statistics (kind 20), not near-surface rate-state parameters (kind 21), but Byerlee-style failure envelopes at seismogenic-zone stresses AND temperatures; the Geology paper's headline is re-derived by the gate on every run: seafloor LITHOLOGY controls strength - clay-rich subduction inputs are uniformly weak (mu <= 0.48 even at 90 MPa / 210 C) while the carbonate-rich material is uniformly strong (mu >= 0.71), a 2.8x mean contrast that maps directly onto where slip instability can nucleate
verified: 31 rows / 237 counted cells against the header's own Size declaration (excluding Event + geocode, EXACT - closes only with u048's sixth stress step); tau = mu x sigma identity re-derived on ALL 31 rows (worst 0.0056 dimensionless, i.e. within published-mu rounding); lithology-contrast headline pinned (11/11 rows of 205-1253 at mu >= 0.71, 20/20 Leg-170 rows at mu <= 0.48, mean ratio 2.79); clay thermal strengthening pinned (u091 90 MPa ambient 0.35 -> u092 90 MPa / 210 C 0.48); ten NaN-index rows disclosed and pinned; gate-pinned; source URL serves the identical dataset
